alignments.note: Imperative with its subject pronoun *ye* under rule 17; *to and fro* is the phrasal rendering of שׁוּט, so the head stays on the lexical verb *Run* by rule 44's phrasal-particle clause.
Preposition בְּ rendered *through*; rule 14's reasoning read off the ASV, applied to a preposition under rule 11.
Construct noun; no article morpheme stands anywhere in the chain (Jerusalem is a bare proper name), so the ASV's supplied *the* joins the construct's unit under rule 29.
Nomen rectum takes the relational *of* under rule 19, headed on the name.
Conjunction waw to *and* (rule 14).
Imperative to *see*.
The particle נָא takes the single word the ASV spends on it, *now*; rule 30's full entreaty formula (*I pray thee*) is not what is written here, so only *now* is aligned.
Conjunction waw to *and* (rule 14).
Imperative to *know*.
Conjunction waw to *and* (rule 14).
Piel imperative to *seek*.
Preposition בְּ to *in* (rule 11).

One substantive rendered by a multi-word phrase: rule 31's subtraction leaves the lexeme on *broad* (*places* alone is any place), as with בָּמָה → *high place*. No article morpheme is present — the noun is determined by its suffix — so the supplied *the* joins this nominal expression under rules 15 and 29. The competing reading heads on *places* as the English head noun; rule 31 expressly rejects that reasoning.
Pronominal suffix to *thereof* (rule 18).
Conditional אִם to *if*.
Finite verb with subject pronoun and modal auxiliary under rule 17, headed on the lexical verb.
Hebrew has no indefinite article, so *a* belongs to the noun it determines (rule 15).
Repeated conditional אִם to the second *if*.

Existential יֵשׁ with the presentative frame *there be*; the dummy *there* belongs to this unit exactly as rule 21 and rule 50 place it, and the head is the lexical anchor *be* rather than the supplied *there*. The following *any* is not taken here: it is the noun phrase the ASV supplies for the anarthrous participle under rule 46.

Anarthrous substantival participle: the supplied *any that* joins its unit under rule 46 and is not `added`, and the head is the word carrying the lexeme, *doeth*. The alternative gives *any* to יֵשׁ as part of the existential frame; rule 46 is preferred because *any* is the antecedent of the relative built on the participle, not part of *there be*.
Object noun מִשְׁפָּט rendered adverbially as *justly*; the ASV's single word for the noun.
Second coordinated anarthrous participle; the ASV writes the antecedent *any* once, so under rule 46's second rider this participle takes only the written *that seeketh*, headed on the lexeme.
אֱמוּנָה to *truth*; the marginal *faithfulness* is a rendering note and does not change the alignment.
Apodosis waw to *and* (rule 14).
Imperfect with subject pronoun and auxiliary under rule 17, headed on *pardon*.
The ASV writes the object bare — *pardon her* — so the dative לְ has no English word of its own (rule 40).
Suffix takes the object pronoun *her* (rules 18 and 40).

review_notes: All 27 source and 43 target tokens are partitioned exactly once.
Two units carry a competing reading in their notes: s013 (*broad places* head) and s020 (whether *any* belongs to יֵשׁ or to the participle).
לְ + suffix is split under rule 40: the preposition is unrepresented and the suffix takes *her*.
